S. Retzlau, alias Karl Groehl.

Was a leading member of the Spartacus League from 1916-18, and did a lot of anti-militarist work during and after the last war. During the Bavarian Soviet Republic he occupied a high post in the Bavarian police. He was arrested several times during and after the last war and underwent several terms of imprisonment. He was one of the founder members of the German Communist Party; up to 1935 he was head of the propagandist publishing concern established by Willi Muenzenberg, who sat in the Reichstag as a Communist. After emigrating, he went over to the Trotskyists and acted as Trotsky's representative for Central Europe, with headquarters in Basel. He went from Switzerland to the Saar, where he spent a year. There he took part in the plebiscite campaign, but broke with Trotsky and went to France, where he placed his services at the disposal of the Deuxième Bureau. He then came to this country with a French passport made out in the name of Retzlau and is said to be doing secret work for a British department. In May, 1942, he founded a "German Federal Socialist Party," which he transformed into the "League of German Revolutionary Socialists" in the following October. Both these organisations never had any real membership list, but Retzlau regards his friends as members. According to the League's programme, the new Germany is to be a federation of socialist, democratic and republican states within the pre-Munich frontiers, but without any central authority. The federal states concerned will be free to secede and join other federations. The German army and police force are to be completely disarmed. The economic structure of Germany is to be a planned socialist economy, with workers' councils, public control of industrial production and a collective system for agriculture. The former German political parties will be deemed to share responsibility for the present German regime and the war. Retzlau's programme shows him to be at variance with the German Communist Party, which he charges with having imitated Nazi methods and institutions.
